title: Processed Foods Offer the Cheapest Calories
description: Created a boxplot visualization using the Grocery Store Foods dataset to examine how food processing relates to affordability. The analysis shows that ultra-processed foods provide the cheapest calories, revealing how economic accessibility often comes at the cost of nutritional quality.

title: Hourly and Seasonal Trends in Marginal Cost of Energy
description: This project analyzes historical Marginal Cost of Energy (MCE) data from 2012–2024 to uncover temporal pricing patterns. The heatmap visualizes average MCE by hour of the day and month, revealing clear daily cycles and stronger seasonal fluctuations. These insights support energy market forecasting and highlight how demand and supply dynamics shift throughout the year.

title: Evaluating Treatment Effectiveness with Qini Curves
description: This project analyzes health data comparing individuals who received a treatment versus those who did not. Using a model trained for treatment effect estimation, we visualized its performance with a Qini curve, which measures how well the model identifies patients most likely to benefit. The curve highlights cumulative gains in outcomes, showing how predictive modeling can support more effective and targeted healthcare interventions.

title: Analyzing the Key Factors in College Admissions Decisions
description: This project explores which factors—GPA, SAT scores, or extracurricular activities—most influence college admission outcomes. Using a Kaggle dataset of 250 students, we analyzed how these variables relate to acceptance, rejection, or waitlist status. Through data cleaning, visualization, and statistical modeling (ANOVA and one-hot encoded linear regression), we found that extracurricular activities show the strongest correlation with acceptance, followed by GPA and SAT scores. The study highlights how non-academic involvement may better reflect student potential than standardized metrics alone, while also discussing ethical issues like bias, fairness, and data privacy in educational data analysis.

title: Predicting Power Outage Severity in the U.S.
description: Analyzed nationwide outage data to identify factors driving severe power losses. Using weather, population, and economic indicators, we built regression models to predict outage severity. Results show that extreme weather and high population density are key predictors, offering insights for improving energy resilience.

title: Addressing Food Insecurity in Yemen — SDG 2: Zero Hunger
description: This project explores the famine crisis in Yemen under the UN’s Zero Hunger goal, focusing on how conflict, inflation, and economic collapse have driven severe food shortages. Drawing on reports from the UN, USAID, and CARE, it highlights humanitarian efforts and the urgent need for sustainable food aid and peacebuilding to combat hunger.
